c1-as-if.title: As If: -gandek
c1-as-if.explanation: Adding dek ("like/as") to the -gan participle creates "as if": u hammasini bilgandek gapirdi (he/she spoke as if he/she knew everything). It expresses a comparison to an event presented as unreal or merely apparent.
c1-as-if.fact: Dek is the same comparative word used in plain similes (sher dek kuchli, "strong as a lion") -- "as if" in Uzbek is grammatically just a simile whose point of comparison happens to be an entire completed action instead of a noun.

dialogue.en: He/she is acting as if nothing happened.

c1-factual-concession.title: Factual Concession: -gani bilan
c1-factual-concession.pattern: [verb stem] + -gan + i + bilan (despite the fact that ~)
c1-factual-concession.explanation: -gani bilan (the -gan participle, possessive -i, plus bilan, "with") concedes a FACT already known to be true, unlike the more hypothetical -sa ham: boy bo'lgani bilan, baxtli emas (despite being rich, he/she isn't happy) presupposes that he/she really is rich.
c1-factual-concession.fact: Because -gani bilan presupposes the conceded fact is real, while -sa ham works for both real and merely hypothetical concessions, native speakers reach for -gani bilan specifically when they want to flag "yes, that part is definitely true, but..." -- a nuance that's easy to blur at lower levels.

dialogue.native: U juda boy-ku, nega xursand emas?
dialogue.en: He/she is very rich, so why isn't he/she happy?
Despite being rich, he/she isn't happy.

c1-embedded-subject.title: Embedded Clause as Subject: -(i)shi
c1-embedded-subject.explanation: A possessive-marked verbal noun lets a whole clause act as the grammatical subject of another sentence: uning kelishi meni xursand qildi ("his/her coming made me happy", i.e. "the fact that he/she came made me happy") -- uning is genitive "his/her", kelishi is "coming" with a matching 3rd-person possessive ending.
c1-embedded-subject.fact: The possessive ending on the verbal noun must agree with whoever performs the embedded action, not with the main sentence's subject -- uning kelishi ("his/her coming") keeps that -i ending no matter who is made happy by it, exactly the way mening kitobim ("my book") agrees with the owner, not the sentence's grammatical subject.

dialogue.native: Uning kelishi meni juda xursand qildi.
dialogue.en: His/her coming made me very happy.

c1-hearsay.title: Hearsay/Doubt: emish
c1-hearsay.explanation: Emish marks reported information the speaker isn't personally vouching for, often with a hint of skepticism: u mashhur olim emish (he/she is allegedly a famous scientist [so I've heard, but I'm not sure]).
c1-hearsay.fact: Emish carries a distancing, sometimes slightly doubtful tone that -deb aytdi (plain reported speech, covered at B1) doesn't -- choosing emish over a neutral report is itself a small signal to the listener that the speaker isn't fully endorsing the claim.

dialogue.en: They say he/she has bought a new car.
Really? He's/she's allegedly a very rich person, apparently.

items.en: He/she spoke as if he/she knew everything.
He/she acted as if nothing had happened.
He/she looked at me as if he/she didn't recognize me.
This task seemed as if it were easy.
He/she continued working as if he/she wasn't tired.
The child spoke as if he/she were an adult.

items.uz: U bu yerni yaxshi bilgandek yurdi.
items.en: He/she walked as if he/she knew this place well.
I felt as if everything was going as planned.
He/she passed by as if he/she hadn't seen me.
It seemed as if I had been here before.
He/she smiled as if he/she wasn't angry.

items.uz: Ish tugagandek ko'rindi, lekin unday emas edi.
items.en: The work seemed as if it were finished, but it wasn't.
Despite being rich, he/she isn't happy.
Despite being young, he/she is very experienced.
Despite being tired, he/she finished the work.
Despite being sick, he/she went to work.

items.uz: Ko'p pul topgani bilan, xursand emas.
items.en: Despite earning a lot of money, he/she isn't happy.

items.uz: Uzr so'ragani bilan, men hali xafaman.
items.en: Despite him/her apologizing, I'm still upset.
Despite being knowledgeable, he/she was humble.

items.uz: Ko'p mashq qilgani bilan, natija bermadi.
items.en: Despite practicing a lot, it didn't yield results.
Despite it being difficult, he/she didn't give up.

items.uz: Mashhur bo'lgani bilan, oddiy hayot kechiradi.
items.en: Despite being famous, he/she leads a simple life.

items.uz: Ko'p vaqt o'tgani bilan, hech narsani unutmadim.
items.en: Despite a lot of time passing, I haven't forgotten anything.

items.uz: Yordam bergani bilan, muammo hal bo'lmadi.
items.en: Despite him/her helping, the problem wasn't resolved.
His/her coming made me happy.

items.uz: Sizning yordam berishingiz juda muhim edi.
items.en: Your helping was very important.

items.uz: Bolaning tez o'sishi meni hayratga soldi.
items.en: The child's fast growth surprised me.

items.uz: Uning bu ishni bajarishi hammani qoyil qoldirdi.
items.en: His/her completing this task impressed everyone.
Your arrival was unexpected.

items.uz: Uning jim qolishi meni tashvishga soldi.
items.en: His/her staying silent worried me.

items.uz: Bizning g'alaba qozonishimiz katta quvonch edi.
items.en: Our winning was a great joy.
His/her speaking silenced everyone.
Your understanding is important to me.

items.uz: Uning kech qolishi odatiy holga aylandi.
items.en: His/her being late became a usual occurrence.

items.uz: Bizning kelishuvga erishishimiz vaqt talab qildi.
items.en: Our reaching an agreement took time.
His/her success inspired us.
He/she is allegedly a famous scientist.
This house is allegedly very expensive.

items.uz: U chet elga ko'chib ketar emish.
items.en: He/she is allegedly moving abroad.
This news is allegedly true.
He/she has allegedly found a new job.
They are allegedly getting divorced.
This movie is allegedly very interesting.
He/she has allegedly won a big prize.
This place is allegedly very dangerous.
He/she allegedly doesn't know about this matter.
There will allegedly be a holiday tomorrow.
He/she allegedly deceives everyone.
